papers.title_en: Design and Evaluation of a Collaborative Teleoperation Interface for Multi-Operator Multi-Robot Systems in Challenging Environments
papers.authors: Alperen Kenan, Juan José García Cárdenas, Adriana Tapus, Paul Bremner, Manuel Giuliani
papers.evidence: 多操作员多机器人协同的协作界面
papers.tldr: 多操作员多机器人遥操作中，异构平台接口不兼容且协作依赖人工沟通，增加认知负荷并限制扩展。研究设计共享可视化协作界面，并用16人实验在核电站数字孪生中比较同地共享、远程共享和同地独立三种条件。同地共享完成任务最快（292.8秒）、碰撞最少（每试次0.9次）、态势感知准确率最高（91.1%），且认知负荷低于远程条件。结果表明同地在场与共享界面可互补支持负荷调节和相互感知，为多操作员多机器人协作提供设计依据。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-robot systems that combine the complementary capabilities of specialised platforms are critical for complex missions in challenging, inaccessible environments. Current deployments assign an operator or operator team to each robot, with collaboration relying on operator-to-operator communication to manually coordinate heterogeneous platforms with incompatible interfaces. This operator-dependent approach increases cognitive load and limits scalability across robots from different manufacturers. This study designs and evaluates a shared-visualisation collaborative teleoperation interface to improve operator coordination, situational awareness, and the task performance in multi-operator, multi-robot systems.   A comparative user study with 16 participants compared three teleoperation conditions: co-located operators with a shared interface, remote operators with a shared interface, and co-located operators with individual interfaces. Participants controlled two simulated robots in a nuclear power plant digital twin to complete disaster response tasks. Performance metrics, physiological data, and behavioural measures were recorded to assess task performance, cognitive load, and operator awareness across conditions. The co-located shared-interface condition achieved the fastest mission completion (292.8 s), outperforming remote operation (351.6 s) and individual interfaces (385.1 s), with the fewest collisions (0.9 per trial) and highest situational awareness accuracy (91.1 %). Physical co-presence was associated with reduced cognitive load, with NASA-TLX scores increasing from 38.2 in co-located to 57.7 in remote operation, supported by consistent physiological indicators. These results demonstrate that co-presence and shared interfaces provide complementary benefits, supporting workload regulation and mutual awareness respectively in multi-operator, multi-robot teleoperation.

papers.title_en: HarnessNet: Feedback-driven Hierarchical Joint Harness Evolution for Multi-agent Systems
papers.authors: Zhaoyuan Qiu, Sachith Seneviratne, Yu Xia, Saman Halgamuge
papers.evidence: 多智能体系统中harness的分层进化优化
papers.tldr: 多智能体系统的联合harness演化尚缺研究，单一全局优化器随规模增长面临上下文和工作负载膨胀及访问限制。HarnessNet以Agentron为基本单元，将可演化前向harness、基础模型与仅能修改本地harness的局部优化器组成分层图，让环境反馈逐层回传并分解联合演化任务。在AgentBench上，多模型实验显示其性能增益与全局优化器相当，同时每次优化调用消耗更少token和时间并保持本地隐私。替换基础模型后演化harness仍具联合有效性，表明跨模型可迁移。
papers.abstract_en: AI agents can evolve by using environment feedback to revise their harnesses, the software managing model inputs, tool use, memory, and execution, while keeping foundation models frozen. Existing studies focus on single agents, leaving joint harness evolution in multi-agent systems (MAS) underexplored. A single global optimizer faces growing context and workload as the system scales, while access restrictions may prevent sharing agent internals or system-wide feedback. We propose HarnessNet, a framework for hierarchical harness evolution in MAS. Its basic unit, Agentron, comprises an evolvable forward harness, a foundation model, and a local optimizer that can observe and modify only that harness. Agentrons form a layered graph through which environment feedback propagates backward, with upstream optimizers receiving node-specific feedback from the downstream layer. This decomposes joint harness evolution into smaller, coordinated tasks with separate contexts, reducing individual optimizers' context and workload while keeping access local. Optimizers need not access all agent trajectories or raw environment feedback. Experiments on AgentBench with multiple foundation models demonstrate the feasibility of training HarnessNet. Compared with a single global optimizer, HarnessNet achieves comparable performance gains while respecting local privacy and requiring fewer tokens and less time per optimizer call. A migration study shows that the evolved harnesses remain jointly effective after replacing the foundation models, suggesting transferability across models.

papers.title_en: Observe, Share, or Predict? Disentangling Partner Information in Embodied Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.authors: Adrián Szlatincsán, Filippo Ziliotto, Bruno Lepri, Luciano Serafini, Massimiliano Luca, Tommaso Campari
papers.evidence: 具身多智能体协作与协调
papers.tldr: LLM作为具身智能体控制器时，无对话团队协作中的伙伴信息作用仍不清楚。作者在PARTNR基准上引入严格个体感知的解耦部分可观测设置，并用OAS观察、KE知识交换和OANA动作预测增强零样本ReAct规划器，在四规划器、1000任务上做2×2×2全网格评估。结果显示OAS提升任务质量并减少无效努力，KE最多缩短25%仿真步数但成功率变化小；OANA在16组中15组降低成功率。协调收益主要来自响应共享上下文尤其是OAS，而非显式预测，伙伴建模较浅且依赖规划器。
papers.abstract_en: LLMs are used as high-level controllers for embodied agents, but it remains unclear whether they support collaborative reasoning, such as anticipating a collaborator's actions in real-time teamwork without dialogue. We ask if observing the partner's state, exchanging object knowledge, and predicting the partner's next action, shape task outcomes and coordination when agents can share percepts but never intentions, plans, or task-level messages, and whether the two agents occupy symmetric roles. Using the Habitat-based PARTNR benchmark, we introduce a Decoupled Partial Observability regime that enforces strictly individual perception, and we augment decentralized zero-shot ReAct planners with Other Agent's State (OAS) observation, object Knowledge Exchange (KE) between co-located agents, and Other Agent's Next Action (OANA) prediction, evaluated on the full 2 x 2 x 2 grid with four planners on 1,000 validation tasks. OAS observation improves task quality, reducing extraneous effort for every planner, whereas KE primarily improves execution efficiency, cutting simulation steps by up to 25% with little change in success. The two are largely redundant for strong planners but complementary for the weakest, for which KE without the OAS is the worst configuration. OANA prediction lowers the success rate in 15 of 16 model x context pairs while raising explicit partner mentions to 55-100%, and its accuracy gains lie mainly in the coarse action type, partly because agents recognize the action the partner is already performing. The robot retrieves objects sooner and completes its tasks earlier than the simulated human. Shared context reduces total task time by shortening the remaining duration that the human works alone. Also, coordination benefits arise from responding to shared context, especially the OAS, rather than explicit anticipation, yielding shallow, planner-dependent partner modeling.

papers.title_en: Degrees of Freedom in Multi-Agent Coordination: Between Centralized and Decentralized Regimes
papers.authors: Yiqing Peng, Hehai Lin, Zixuan Wang, Dongyi Zhang, Zhengjie Zhu, Yi Han, Yangyang Zheng, Hao Wang, Qian Li, Chengwei Qin
papers.evidence: 用连续自由度框架研究集中式与分散式多智能体协调机制
papers.tldr: LLM多智能体常采用集中式或分散式协调，前者有瓶颈、后者依赖分布式决策。本文提出自由度（DoF）连续配置框架，量化下放给下游智能体的决策空间，并调节任务粒度与分支分配概率，两端可还原两种协调模式。多任务实验显示性能格局随任务域变化，六个评估状态中有五个的中间DoF配置平均准确率高于两端。该工作为设计与研究居间协调机制提供了实证依据。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) are commonly organized around two coordination regimes. Centralized coordination provides explicit control but can create a bottleneck at a single coordination locus, whereas decentralized coordination offers local autonomy but must achieve effective collaboration through distributed decisions and experience. These trade-offs motivate a systematic study of the space between the two regimes. We introduce Degrees of Freedom (DoF), a continuous configuration framework that quantifies the size of the decision space delegated to downstream agents. DoF controls the granularity of delegated work and the target probability that each task unit is assigned to the branches. Its endpoints recover the two coordination regimes. Across multiple task domains, DoF reveals a hierarchy of organizational effects. Delegated granularity and within-regime routing produce structured but bounded profile reallocations, whereas task domain and retained experience are associated with stronger differences between the centralized- and decentralized-branch profiles. The resulting performance landscape is task-dependent: different domains favor different DoF configurations, while atomic-target conditions are more consistent across runs. In-domain retained experience brings the two branch profiles closer together. The same controlled sweep reveals a task-dependent coordination landscape: some domains exhibit higher-performing configurations, whereas others show flatter responses and no single configuration dominates across domains. In five of the six evaluated state, an intermediate DoF configuration achieves higher mean accuracy than both endpoints, demonstrating the value of exploring the coordination space between them. Together, these findings provide empirical guidance for studying and designing intermediate coordination regimes in LLM-based MAS.
